definitions.gloss: farewell gift; parting gift; going-away present (often money)
definitions.explanation: A gift, typically money in an envelope, given to someone who is moving away, transferring to another workplace, or embarking on a long journey.

examples.japanese: {餞別|せんべつ}をいただいた。
{転勤|てんきん}する{同僚|どうりょう}に{餞別|せんべつ}を{贈|おく}った。
examples.english: I gave a farewell gift to a colleague being transferred.

examples.japanese: {留学|りゅうがく}に{行|い}く{前|まえ}に、{職場|しょくば}の{皆|みな}さんから{餞別|せんべつ}として{現金|げんきん}をいただいた。
examples.english: Before leaving to study abroad, I received cash as a farewell gift from everyone at work.

notes:
Written with the character {餞|せん} (farewell feast) + {別|べつ} (parting). Traditionally, {餞別|せんべつ} often takes the form of money placed in a special envelope, though it can also be a physical gift.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {餞別|せんべつ}を{贈|おく}る — to give a farewell gift
- {餞別|せんべつ}をいただく — to receive a farewell gift (humble)
- {餞別|せんべつ}を{渡|わた}す — to hand over a farewell gift
- {餞別|せんべつ}{品|ひん} — farewell gift item

CULTURAL NOTE:
Giving {餞別|せんべつ} is a well-established Japanese custom, particularly in workplaces. When a colleague is transferred ({転勤|てんきん}), retiring ({退職|たいしょく}), or going on a long trip, coworkers typically collect money and present it in a {祝儀袋|しゅうぎぶくろ} (ceremonial envelope). The amount varies by relationship closeness, typically ranging from 3,000 to 10,000 yen.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- はなむけ — farewell words or gift (more literary; can refer to encouraging words as well as gifts)
- {送別|そうべつ}{品|ひん} — farewell gift (more general, less traditional nuance)
